provenance.note: Place name on the river, geocoded to the reach [supplied on this invocation]
Steady upstream CARRIER discharge - the river flow that dilutes and transports the release [supplied on this invocation]
Result-writing cadence; unset keeps the steering file's own period [supplied on this invocation]
Modeled reach length downstream of the release; a longer reach is coarsened under the mesh node budget [supplied on this invocation]
Where the substance enters the water, as a Point: the pick's {coordinates, name} verbatim, a (lon, lat) pair, 'lat,lon', a point layer, or a place name [supplied on this invocation]
Finite injection window; the substance is released over it and the rest of the run is what happens to what was released [supplied on this invocation]
Discharge of the release itself - with the carrier flow this sets the dilution the reach receives [supplied on this invocation]
DISSOLVED concentration of the substance in the release itself, before any dilution; everything that ends up on sediment gets there by sorption during the run [supplied on this invocation]

Suspended sediment the river already carries, in and at the top of the reach. It is the SORBENT: with none, the substance stays dissolved and nothing reaches the bed. Nothing fetches suspended sediment for a reach, so this is a STATED condition, not a measured one - state the gauged value if the reach has one [supplied on this invocation]
Along-reach position the history is read at when no point was given, 0=upstream..1=downstream [supplied on this invocation]

Simulated time. Sorption equilibrates in hours and settling takes longer than that, so a window of a few hours reports a partition that has not happened yet; two days is what the default covers [supplied on this invocation]
Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; peak concentration is a resolution-bound class and a coarse mesh reads it low [supplied on this invocation]
Solve sizing class [declared constant default]

Along-reach release position, 0=upstream..1=downstream; the source must sit strictly INSIDE the reach, never on a boundary. It sits near the top so the substance has reach left to sorb and settle in [declared scenario default]

not supplied; the engine's own sediment settling velocity, 6e-6 m/s, stands
